newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian oil official cites security fears.
newsitem.headline: Colombian oil official cites security fears.

text.p: BOGOTA, April 15 Reuter - The head of the state oil company, Ecopetrol, said foreign investment in Colombia's oil sector could come to a standstill unless the government succeeds in addressing the mounting security concerns of multinationals like British Petroleum Co Plc.
"Today, all investment in the oil sector depends on the government's commitment to increase security," said Ecopetrol president Antonio Urdinola.
"Foreign investors are hysterical when it comes to security in Colombia," he added.

Energy and Minies Minister Rodrigo Villamizar said BP director general John Browne warned the government during a visit to Bogota last month that increasing leftist guerrilla activity could force the company to abandon some of its oil exploration projects in Colombia.
Urdinola, who spoke in an interview published in Tuesday's editions of Bogota's El Tiempo newspaper, said the problem went beyond BP, however.
"It's not just BP, all the oil companies are extremely concerned," he said.

He added that the government was firmly committed to ensuring better protection for companies working under association contracts with Ecopetrol but gave no specifics as to what might actually be done.

Military officials have complained in the past that up to one third of the country's thinly stretched army, with a combat force just 100,000-strong, is tied up guarding oil and coal facilities and infrastructure across the country. They have also complained that the cash-strapped government has failed to provide the armed forces with adequate financial support.
